Values, Vision, Ethos
Achieve, Inspire, Succeed
Alexandra Infant School Motto
Our Motto And Vision
Our school motto is Achieve, Inspire, Succeed. This motto encompasses the aspirations that we have for all of our children. We provide inspirational learning experiences and celebrate every child’s individual achievement. Personal and academic success is supported by and shared with Alexandra Infant community including children, parents, carers, staff, governors and friends.
At Alexandra Infant School we are passionate about developing the ‘whole child’. Teaching life skills that will enable children to thrive, not only in our school, but throughout their education and into adult life.
Through our motto we encourage children to understand and develop our core values:
Be resilient
Be respectful
Be confident
Be caring
Aims
At Alexandra Infant School we are dedicated to providing high quality education which will enable all children to enjoy learning and to achieve their personal best.
We do this through:
The staff at Alexandra Infant School have all contributed and share these aims and these are echoed through conversations with children, parents and Local Committee Members.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - Alexandra Infant School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
A warm welcome to Alexandra Infant School, where we are passionate about learning and celebrating individual achievements.
We are a two-form entry infant school with an Additionally Resourced Provision for children with autism. There is access to wrap around care before and after school. All children at Alexandra Infant School automatically gain a place at Alexandra Junior School and we work very closely with the Junior School to ensure a smooth transition into KS2 for our Year 2 children.
At Alexandra Infant School, we pride ourselves on developing the ‘whole child’, teaching life skills that will enable children to thrive, not only in our school, but throughout their education and into adult life.
Our nurturing school provides a safe learning environment where all children can thrive and reach their full potential. The well-being of children and staff is our highest priority, and we work closely with our families and the community to achieve this. We have strong home-school links and parents and carers play a key role in enabling every child to succeed.
Our motto ‘Achieve, Inspire, Succeed’ encompasses the aspirations that we have for all of our children. We provide inspirational and inclusive learning experiences and celebrate every child’s individual achievement. Personal and academic success is supported by and shared with the Alexandra Infant community including children, families, staff and Local Committee Members.
Having gained the Inclusion Quality Mark in recognition of our excellent practice, we are dedicated to providing high quality education which will enable all children to enjoy learning and to achieve their personal best. Our curriculum provides specialist teachers and there is a range of extra-curricular activities that further enrich our broad and balanced curriculum. Children are challenged throughout their learning and encouraged to ask questions, solve problems, build resilience, and become independent learners. There is also the opportunity for children to learn the violin, piano or cello if they choose to.
The Local Committee Members in our school have a wide range of skills and experience in order to support the school and drive school improvement. They are committed to ensuring the very best outcomes for all of our children.
Miss Alison Hills - Head Teacher
Further Information About Alexandra Infant School
All children at Alexandra Infant School will automatically gain a place at Alexandra Junior School. We work very closely with the Junior School to ensure a smooth transition into KS2 for our Year 2 children. If you would like to find out about the Junior School, please follow this link:
Alexandra Junior School

pageCache.pageTitle: Supporting British Values - Alexandra Infant School
pageCache.text:
Supporting British Values
At Alexandra Infant School we take very seriously our responsibility to prepare children for modern life in Britain, a duty set out by Government. The Government emphasises that schools are required to ensure that key ‘British Values’ are taught in all UK schools. We ensure that the Fundamental British Values are introduced, discussed and lived out through the work and ethos of our school. All curriculum areas provide a vehicle for further understanding of these concepts and, in particular, our RE and PSHE lessons provide excellent opportunities to deepen and develop understanding. Children embrace these concepts with enthusiasm and demonstrate a good understanding of their application to their own lives.
The school makes considerable efforts to ensure children have exposure to a wide experience beyond their local community during which these concepts are shown, through for example sporting events and visits. Their strong rooted values-based understanding gives them an excellent platform for embracing difference.
By actively promoting British Values we aim to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Children are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subjects to its law.
The Key Values are:
British-Values-Poster.pdfHow we Teach Key Values
Democracy
Rule of Law
Individual Liberty
Mutual Respect

Music
"Where words fail, music speaks"
Hans Christian Andersen
Every child has the right to relax, play and take part in a wide range of cultural and artistic activities. Article 31 Every child has the right to an education. Article 28 Music is essentially a practical subject which should be enjoyed by all. Our intent is to engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement. From an early age children have an awareness of rhythm, pitch and sounds around them and these should be developed on entry to school. Music is taught both inside and outside the classroom and is fully inclusive of children of differing abilities.

"Every child is an artist"

We encourage pupils to be creative and imaginative and to explore the tactile, visual and sensory qualities of the arts, through the teaching of specific skills and techniques, and also through cross-curricular work. Art is taught both inside and outside the classroom and is fully inclusive of children of differing abilities.

English
"There is always room for a story that can transport people to another place"
At Alexandra Infant School we firmly believe that English is at the heart of all learning. By equipping children with the ability to listen, speak, read and write confidently, they will be able to access all areas of learning and will have the solid foundations to grow as confident independent learners. Speaking, listening, reading and writing is embedded across all areas of the curriculum. At Alexandra Infant School teaching takes place through a creative, broad and balanced curriculum. This ensures that children are exposed to, through theme based learning, a rich variety of language, both in the spoken and written form. Children enter Alexandra Infant School with varying levels of linguistic and fluency skills. Through comprehensive planning, each child is provided with a personalised platform to develop their speaking, listening, reading and writing throughout their infant years.

pageCache.text:
Geography
Geography.pdf"Once a year, go somewhere you've never been before"
A high-quality geography education should inspire in pupils a curiosity and fascination about the world and its people that will remain with them for the rest of their lives. Teaching should equip pupils with knowledge about diverse places, people, resources and natural and human environments, together with a deep understanding of the Earth’s key physical and human processes. As pupils progress, their growing knowledge about the world should help to deepen their understanding of the interaction between physical and human processes, and of the formation and use of landscapes and environments. Geographical knowledge, understanding and skills provide the framework and approaches that explain how the Earth’s features at different scales are shaped, interconnected and change over time.

pageCache.text:
PE
"Always train hard, work harder, never give in and believe in you."
Alexandra Infant School recognises the important contribution of physical education (PE) in a child’s physical, cognitive, social and emotional development. We believe that physical education develops the children’s knowledge, skills and understanding of physical activities. These include dance, team and individual games, gymnastics, football, volleyball, tennis and athletics, engaging children in activities both indoors and outside. It also includes stretch, balance and mindfulness which contributes that their physical and mental wellbeing, promoting strategies to support children in their behaviour for learning and social skills. Physical education encourages the children to gain a greater understanding of their bodies in action and also involves them in selecting and applying skills and promoting positive attitudes towards a healthy lifestyle. Therefore, we enable the children to be able to make informed choices about physical activity throughout their lives. It also encourages healthy competition in and out of school as well as highlighting the importance of team building, fair play, rules and boundaries. All PE sessions at AIS are fully inclusive and include all children of differing abilities. Provision is made for SEN children in the school. PE is a real opportunity for both teachers and children to consolidate and work on the values that underpin every aspect of school life with purposeful and inspirational teaching and learning.

"Technology is best when it brings people together"

History
"The more you know about the past the better prepared you are for the future"
We aim to teach children to understand how past events have influenced our lives today and encourage children, through investigation, to develop the skills of enquiry, analysis, interpretation and problem-solving. We believe providing children with exciting, engaging links with the community and memorable experiences enhances their learning. Through this, pupils gain a coherent knowledge and understanding of Britain’s past and that of the wider world. It should inspire pupils’ curiosity to know more about the past. History helps pupils to understand the complexity of people’s lives, the process of change, the diversity of societies and relationships between different groups, as well as their own identity and the challenges of their time.

PSHE
"A little consideration, a little thought for others, makes all the difference"
At AIS, we are committed to ensuring that the emotional and social needs of all our children are met, as well as supporting the development of children’s health and wellbeing, self-esteem and confidence. We provide a broad and balanced PSHE curriculum through our agreed PSHE whole school approach. We nurture and support Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural development in young children and promote fundamental British Values. We support children in developing the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to lead confident, healthy and independent lives and become responsible citizens. We recognise that our school vision is crucial to this learning and should be at the heart of whole school development. It is important for us to deliver this curriculum in a range of inspiring ways so that the children are able to: -celebrate differences and multi-cultural diversity -develop crucial life skills, such as building independence, confidence and teamwork -broaden their opportunities and experiences through a range of indoor and outdoor learning, -access the curriculum through a range of multi-sensory, practical and hands on experiences -engage in creative, topic based discussions that provoke their curiosity and understanding of local and global environmental issues -provide a safe and welcoming vocabulary rich environment to extend communication skills and develop their ability to ask questions.

DT
"You can't use up creativity. The more you use, the more you have"
Design Technology is an inspiring, rigorous and practical subject. We encourage pupils to use creativity and imagination to design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts; considering their own and others’ needs, wants and values. Children acquire a broad range of subject knowledge and draw on disciplines such as Mathematics, Science, Engineering, Computing and Art. DT is taught both inside and outside the classroom and is fully inclusive of children of differing abilities.

Maths
"There is a difference between not knowing and not knowing yet"
We aim to inspire all our pupils, irrespective of their ability, to reach their full academic potential in all subjects. We recognise that mathematics is a critical area of skill and knowledge that impacts on the quality and value of the lives we lead. Therefore, our objectives in the teaching of the maths curriculum include: • Promoting enjoyment of learning through practical activity, outdoor learning, exploration and discussion; • Developing confidence and competence with numbers and the number system; • Developing children’s ability to solve a variety of problems through decision-making and reasoning in a range of contexts; • Developing a practical understanding of the ways in which information is gathered and presented; • Exploring features of shape and space, and developing measuring skills in a range of contexts; • Helping children understand the importance of mathematics in everyday life • Encouraging explanation, reasoning, justification and routine and non-routine problem solving across a range of contexts.

RE
"There are many cultural differences between us, but I think we'll find a lot of similarities too"
Every child has the right to relax, play and take part in a wide range of cultural and artistic activities: Article 31. Every child has the right to an education: Article 28. It is our intent for the RE curriculum at Alexander Infant School to engage, inspire, challenge and encourage pupils, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to answer challenging questions through a curriculum that is accessible to all. At AIS, R.E. is taught in line with the statutory requirements of the Early Years Foundation Stage and National Curriculum. We follow the Bromley RE syllabus which encourages children to explore and express their own responses and personal beliefs. AIS provides opportunities for children to: • Develop knowledge and understanding of Christianity and of the other religions represented in Great Britain • Understand and make links between the beliefs, practices and value systems of different faiths • Develop an interest in and enthusiasm for the study of religion and enhance their own spiritual, moral, social and cultural development • Develop the ability to make reasoned, informed and creative responses to religious and moral issues.
